body:
Alas this is an intended behavior mostly. In Google, we just have one version of everything so we don't run into that problem...

I don't really have a good answer on how to fix that for now.

issue.title: Inlined jars in bazel_tools jar conflicting with our libraries

labels.name: P2
labels.description: We'll consider working on this in future. (Assignee optional)

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
Hello!

We have some conflicts with inlined jars in bazel_tools.jar conflicting with the jars that we're using. For example, we depend on the version of Guice that includes AOP support, but the inlined version in bazel_tools.jar is listed first on the classpath.

This is probably the same root cause as #1150, but presents with a different error.

Example error:

```
java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: redfin.util.statsd.StatsdModule.bindInterceptor(Lcom/google/inject/matcher/Matcher;Lcom/google/inject/matcher/Matcher;[Lorg/aopalliance/intercept/MethodInterceptor;)V
    at redfin.util.statsd.StatsdModule.configure(StatsdModule.java:359)
    at com.google.inject.AbstractModule.configure(AbstractModule.java:62)
    at com.google.inject.spi.Elements$RecordingBinder.install(Elements.java:340)
    at com.google.inject.spi.Elements.getElements(Elements.java:110)
    at com.google.inject.internal.InjectorShell$Builder.build(InjectorShell.java:138)
    at com.google.inject.internal.InternalInjectorCreator.build(InternalInjectorCreator.java:104)
    at com.google.inject.Guice.createInjector(Guice.java:96)
    at com.google.inject.Guice.createInjector(Guice.java:73)
    at com.google.inject.Guice.createInjector(Guice.java:62)
    at redfin.stingray.accountManager.FacebookLoginControllerTest.<init>
... <snip> ...
com.google.testing.junit.runner.junit4.CancellableRequestFactory$CancellableRunner.run(CancellableRequestFactory.java:84)
    at org.junit.runner.JUnitCore.run(JUnitCore.java:160)
    at org.junit.runner.JUnitCore.run(JUnitCore.java:138)
    at com.google.testing.junit.runner.junit4.JUnit4Runner.run(JUnit4Runner.java:103)
    at com.google.testing.junit.runner.BazelTestRunner.runTestsInSuite(BazelTestRunner.java:149)
    at com.google.testing.junit.runner.BazelTestRunner.main(BazelTestRunner.java:90)
```

body: We could jarjar the guava dependency of the test runner, or rewrite the code to not depend on guava in the first place. Rewriting is a bunch of work, even if none of the individual dependencies is particularly complex or difficult to remove. We'd also have to make it work with our internal modifications. I guess that means jarjar or proguard time.
Actually, it doesn't look too difficult to remove the remaining uses of guava, but it's possible I'm missing something.

issue.title: tools/jdk/TestRunner_deploy.jar pollutes the classpath for java_test targets

labels.name: P2
labels.description: We'll consider working on this in future. (Assignee optional)

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
tools/jdk/TestRunner_deploy.jar includes guava 19.0, which creates conflicts for any workspaces that attempt to use a different version of guava (i.e. 20.0-SNAPSHOT).

I've put together a sample project that can reproduce the problem with bazel 0.3.1:

https://github.com/jleyba/bazel-classpath
